prs.title: [compiler] Allow ref access in ResizeObserver / MutationObserver callbacks
prs.author: zhoubiao188
prs.body:
## Summary

`new ResizeObserver(() => ref.current)` and `new MutationObserver(() => ref.current)` currently report a false positive:

```
Error: Cannot access refs during render
  > 6 |   return new ResizeObserver(() => ref.current);
      |                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render
```

Both constructors only *retain* the callback and invoke it asynchronously after the observation fires — never during render — so reading a ref inside the callback is safe. The same reasoning was applied to `IntersectionObserver` in #37764; the remaining two DOM observer constructors were still unmodeled and fell back to the default effects for unknown constructors.

This PR models both the same way in the TypeScript and Rust compilers:

- `ResizeObserver(callback)`: single `Freeze`d callback. (Unlike `IntersectionObserver`, whose options object is a second constructor argument, the `{box}` option of `ResizeObserver` belongs to `observe(target, options)`.)
- `MutationObserver(callback)`: single `Freeze`d callback.

## Validation

- `allow-ref-access-in-resize-observer.ts`: plain callback compiles, and `observe(target, {box})` options do not trip the validation.
- `allow-ref-access-in-mutation-observer.ts`: callback compiles.
- `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-resize-observer.js`: mutating a `useMemo` value inside the callback is **still** rejected (`This value cannot be modified`), i.e. the `Freeze` effect is preserved and onl

prs.title: [compiler] Retain declared Freeze effects on already-frozen values for ref validation
prs.author: Gourav224
prs.body:
## Summary

When an operand is already frozen (e.g. a memoized value), `applyEffect` drops a declared `Freeze` effect because nothing new gets frozen. Ref validation reads the declared `Freeze` effects of known signatures, so it misses them in this case. For example, with `PanResponder.create`'s signature:

```js
const ref = useRef(0);
const config = useMemo(() => ({onPanResponderRelease: () => { ref.current = 0; }}), []);
const responder = PanResponder.create(config); // false positive: ref access reported
```

This keeps the declared effect on the instruction when the value is already frozen, as suggested by @javache in #37970. This is metadata only: nothing extra is frozen.

**Note:** the literal diff from review (always `effects.push(effect)`) regressed 11 snapshot fixtures. A retained `Freeze` sets `operand.effect === Effect.Freeze` in `InferMutationAliasingRanges`, which `ValidateNoFreezingKnownMutableFunctions` reads, so it started reporting an extra "Cannot modify local variables after render completes" error on already-frozen operands. It also made the valid `allow-mutate-global-in-effect-fixpoint` fixture fail, and added a duplicate error to e.g. `error.assign-ref-in-effect-hint`, `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-intersection-observer` and `error.todo-reassign-const`.

So this PR keeps the effect for ref validation only: the retained effect is marked `alreadyFrozen`, and `InferMutationAliasingRanges` skips it when computing operand effects. All other passes see w
